title: S&P 500 Earnings Growth to Slow as AI Spending Cools
summary: Goldman Sachs forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth will decelerate as corporate AI infrastructure spending momentum weakens, signaling a shift in 2026.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Goldman Sachs forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth will decelerate as corporate AI infrastructure spending momentum weakens through 2026.
- Big Tech capital expenditure on data centers and chips has peaked, signaling a shift from expansion to optimization.
- The forecast reflects a maturation phase where AI investments transition from infrastructure buildout to revenue-generating applications.


Goldman Sachs has issued a sobering forecast for U.S. equity markets, predicting that S&P 500 earnings growth will decelerate as the surge in corporate AI infrastructure spending loses momentum. Officially released on November 1, 2026, the investment bank's analysis signals a turning point for the AI investment cycle that has driven extraordinary growth in technology stocks over the past three years.


## Peak AI Infrastructure Spending


The forecast centers on a fundamental shift in how companies are allocating capital toward artificial intelligence. According to Goldman's research team, Big Tech firms including Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta have reached peak spending rates on data centers, specialized chips, and GPU clusters. While these companies poured record sums into AI infrastructure throughout 2024 and 2025, the pace of new capital commitments is now moderating as existing facilities come online and utilization rates stabilize.


This transition reflects a natural evolution in technology investment cycles. The initial infrastructure buildout phase, characterized by explosive growth in capital expenditure, is giving way to an optimization phase where companies focus on extracting returns from existing assets rather than expanding capacity at breakneck speed.


## Implications for Market Earnings


Goldman's analysts project that the slowdown in AI-related capital spending will directly impact S&P 500 earnings growth rates in coming quarters. Technology sector earnings, which have consistently beaten expectations due to AI tailwinds, are likely to see more modest gains. The ripple effects extend beyond Big Tech to semiconductor manufacturers, cloud service providers, and enterprise software companies that benefited from the infrastructure boom.


The forecast does not suggest an outright decline in AI investment. Rather, Goldman expects spending growth rates to normalize from unsustainable peaks. Companies will continue investing in AI, but the year-over-year percentage increases will moderate as comparison bases become more challenging and strategic priorities shift toward monetization rather than pure capacity expansion.


## Release Date and Market Context


Goldman Sachs officially released this earnings forecast on November 1, 2026, positioning it ahead of the Q4 earnings season when many technology companies will report full-year results. The timing allows investors to recalibrate expectations before the traditional year-end rally period. Market reactions have been mixed, with value stocks gaining ground relative to growth names that had priced in continued AI spending acceleration.


The forecast aligns with recent commentary from other Wall Street firms observing similar trends. Several Big Tech executives have signaled in recent earnings calls that while AI remains a strategic priority, the pace of infrastructure expansion will moderate as they focus on improving margins and demonstrating return on invested capital.


## Broader Economic Signals


Beyond the immediate impact on equity valuations, Goldman's forecast carries implications for the broader economy. The AI infrastructure boom has supported job growth in construction, manufacturing, and technology services. A slowdown in capital spending could moderate employment gains in these sectors, though the analysts note that operational spending on AI talent and software development continues to grow robustly.


Goldman also highlighted that the maturation of AI infrastructure creates opportunities in different market segments. Companies providing AI application software, implementation services, and vertical-specific solutions may see accelerated growth as enterprises shift from building infrastructure to deploying productive AI systems. This rotation could support continued earnings growth in the technology sector, albeit with a different composition of winners.


## What This Means


Goldman Sachs' forecast marks an inflection point in the AI investment narrative that has dominated markets since late 2022. While the projection of slower earnings growth may disappoint momentum investors, it reflects a healthy transition from speculative infrastructure buildout to sustainable business models. The companies best positioned for this next phase will be those demonstrating clear paths to monetization rather than simply scaling capacity. For investors, the message is clear: the easy money from AI infrastructure spending has been made, and selectivity will matter more than broad exposure to the theme going forward.
